newsitem.title: TURKEY: First tanker loaded with Iraq oil leaves Turk port.
newsitem.headline: First tanker loaded with Iraq oil leaves Turk port.

text.p: The first tanker carrying Iraqi oil left the Ceyhan terminal on Turkey's southern coast on Monday after being filled with 153,500 tonnes of Kirkuk crude, oil officials said.

Fatih Sen, regional director of state pipeline company Botas, said the Gole tanker had left the 1,900-metre jetty at the port -- the terminus for the 986-km twin pipeline from the Kirkuk oilfields -- for Turkey's western refinery of Aliaga.

The tanker was loaded with oil purchased by Turkey's state oil refiner Tupras, one of the five companies so far to have obtained approval from the United Nations to buy oil under the oil-for-food deal.

Turkey's Prime Minister and several other government ministers and officials attended a ceremony to mark the first loading of oil from the terminal on a tanker after a six-year shutdown of the pipeline due to a U.N. embargo on Iraq.
